problem_text:
A logistics manager is selecting cargo containers to load onto a transport vessel. Available containers are:

* Container 1: weight 35 tons, revenue 223 units
* Container 2: weight 17 tons, revenue 16 units
* Container 3: weight 49 tons, revenue 197 units
* Container 4: weight 9 tons, revenue 32 units
* Container 5: weight 33 tons, revenue 120 units
* Container 6: weight 46 tons, revenue 237 units
* Container 7: weight 43 tons, revenue 148 units
* Container 8: weight 50 tons, revenue 223 units
* Container 9: weight 50 tons, revenue 40 units
* Container 10: weight 49 tons, revenue 137 units
* Container 11: weight 38 tons, revenue 146 units
* Container 12: weight 13 tons, revenue 182 units
* Container 13: weight 43 tons, revenue 63 units
* Container 14: weight 45 tons, revenue 147 units
* Container 15: weight 32 tons, revenue 200 units
* Container 16: weight 19 tons, revenue 39 units
* Container 17: weight 17 tons, revenue 65 units
* Container 18: weight 23 tons, revenue 155 units
* Container 19: weight 13 tons, revenue 184 units
* Container 20: weight 15 tons, revenue 133 units
* Container 21: weight 13 tons, revenue 106 units
* Container 22: weight 44 tons, revenue 203 units

The vessel has a maximum cargo capacity of 487 tons. Choose the combination of containers that maximizes total revenue without exceeding this weight limit. Each container must be either fully loaded or left behind.
